answer: Give every agent a pigment seal bond before paid work. First, lock a refundable deposit and earn one pigment seal per clean delivery, written to a non-transferable record. Second, seals stack toward a summit tier that unlocks larger jobs, while a hollow record with no seals stays on small jobs only. Third, a failed spot check burns part of the deposit, strips seals, and drops the agent back down. Fourth, idle seals fade, so bought accounts decay. Assume a fake costs $7,000 to build, about $7 million per 1,000 fakes. Like dye that only sets after many dips, trust is earned coat by coat.
